Outcome_variable.extract_value: life satisfaction, positive affect, negative affect
Outcome_variable.evidence_source: [/page/11/Text/2] Although the instruments used to measure LS, PA, and NA showed high reliability, appropriate measures for the three constructs have been developed and validated for use with adolescents (e.g., the Students' life Satisfaction Scale by Huebner 1991b; the PANAS-C by Laurent et al. 1999). Nevertheless, evidence of the reliability and validity of the SWLS and the PANAS in adolescents can be found elsewhere (SWLS: Proctor et al. 2009. PANAS: Huebner and Dew 1995; McCullough et al. 2000).

sample_type.evidence_source: [/page/11/Text/2] The version of the TCI used in the present study was found more appropriate because the participants in the present study were high-school pupils with an age range from 15 to 18.

lag.evidence_source: [/page/10/Text/7] The present study was based on self-reports and only over 1 year. Thus, an experimental approach and studies conducted from early adolescence to the transition of adolescence [/page/11/Text/1] may add some strength to the findings presented here. It is plausible to question why personality was measured only at T1 if character actually changes with age. However, the time span between T1 and T2 was considered to be relatively short to show significant changes in character—character seems, namely, to be more stable among older adolescents (Schmeck et al. 2001).
